newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soy products end lower as wheat collapses.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soy products end lower as wheat collapses.

text.p: CBOT soy product futures closed lower on a late collapse in wheat, traders said.
The lower close occurred despite bullish export news.
USDA early Thursday released a bullish weekly export sales summary for the soy complex and U.S. Midwest weather remained adverse to harvesting of the U.S. soybean crop.

ADM Investor Services bought 300 December soymeal, 200 January, 200 March and 200 July, traders said. In soyoil Cargill Inc bought 300 lots each of December and January while Term Commodities bought 700 lots of December, traders said.
Soymeal futures volume was estimated at 29,000 contracts, up from 19,751 Wednesday, according to the CBOT. Soyoil options volume was estimated by USDA at 21,000 contracts, up from 16,249 Wednesday.
Soyoil closed 0.27 to 0.34 cent per lb lower, with December down 0.27 at 23.26 cents. Soymeal was $1.00 to $2.00 per ton lower, with December down $1.00 at $227.20.
